questions.question: Describe the procedure of titrating oxalic acid solution with standard KMn O4. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the procedure of titrating oxalic acid solution with standard KMnO4
  • Pipette out oxalic acid into conical flask., Add dilute H₂SO₄ and warm to 60–70°C.
  • Titrate with KMnO₄ until permanent pink colour persists.
  • Reaction: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O. (Correct procedure -give 4
  • marks)

questions.question: Why is it important to use a filter paper of appropriate pore size during filtration? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is it important to use a filter paper of appropriate pore size during filtration?
  • Large pore size-Fine particles may pass through, leading to a turbid filtrate, Small pore size -
  • Filtration becomes slow or may clog. Right pore size ensures optimal flow rate without
  • compromising the removal of unwanted solids, it balances speed and precision, especially
  • important in time-sensitive or high-throughput workflows, inappropriate pore size can lead
  • to loss of analyte or contamination of the filtrate (Any five valid points give 7 marks)

questions.solution_html:

  • Heating a liquid mixture to separate components based on differences in boiling points, Pour
  • the liquid mixture to be distilled into the round-bottom flask. Add boiling chips to promote
  • smooth boiling and prevent bumping, Gradually heat the flask using a h eating mantle or
  • water bath, Monitor the temperature with the thermometer placed at the distillation head,
  • As the mixture reaches the boiling point of the more volatile component, it vaporizes,
  • Vapors enter the condenser, which is cooled by circulating wat er. The vapor condenses
  • back into liquid form. (Explanation with steps-give 7 marks)

questions.question: Describe the principle of reverse phase chromatography and how it differs from normal phase chromatography. / [CO4] [7x5 = 35]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the principle of reverse phase chromatography and how it differs from
  • normal phase chromatography.
  • Liquid chromatography technique used to separate compounds based on hydrophobicity
  • Reverse-phase Chromatography-Stationary Phase: Non-polar (typically silica modified with
  • long-chain alkyl groups like C18), Mobile Phase: Polar solvents, Mechanism: Polar
  • compounds elute faster because they interact less with the non -polar stationary phase.
  • Normal-phase chromatography -Stationary Phase: Polar (e.g., unmodified silica or
  • alumina).Mobile Phase: Non-polar solvents (e.g., hexane, chloroform).Mechanism: Polar
  • compounds are retained longer due to strong interactions with the polar stationary phas e.
  • Non-polar compounds elute faster (Principle -2 marks, Any 2 differences: 5 marks)

questions.question: Discuss the concepts of mean, variance, and standard deviation, including their mathematical formulas and applications in statistical analysis and data interpretation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the concepts of mean, variance, and standard deviation,including their
  • mathematical formulas and applications in statistical analysis and data interpretation
  • Mean (x̄ ): Average of all observations, Formula: x̄ = Σx / n.
  • Represents central tendency of data.
  • Variance (s²): Measure of data spread around mean, Formula: s² = Σ(x − x̄ )² / (n − 1).
  • Standard Deviation (s): Square root of variance., Formula: s = √s².
  • Indicates precision and reliability of measurements.
  • Smaller s → higher precision; larger s → greater variation.
  • Used in data interpretation, error analysis, and quality control.
  • (Mean, variance, and standard deviation definition with mathematical formulas: 3+3+3;
  • Any one application for each: 2+2+2 marks)

questions.question: Briefly discuss the basic principle and procedure of (a) Direct titration (b) Indirect titration (c) Back titration (d) Replacement titration / [CO3] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Briefly discuss the basic principle and procedure of (a) Direct titration(b) Indirect titration
  • (c) Back titration (d) Replacement titration
  • a) Direct: Titrant reacts directly with analyte. Metal ion in solution reacts directly with EDTA to form
  • a stable complex.
  • Take the metal ion solution (e.g., Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺),Add suitable buffer (pH ≈ 10) and indicator (Eriochrome
  • Black T).Titrate with standard EDTA until color changes from wine red to blue.
  • Calculate metal ion concentration from volume of EDTA used
  • b) Indirect: Used for estimation of ions such as Sulphate, Phosphate etc. which do not directly react
  • with EDTA. These ions first converted to metallic salts ( like BaSO4) by adding excess metal ion
  • solutions (Ba2+) and then excess metal ion is titrated with EDTA.
  • c)Back titration: Used when direct titration is slow or incomplete. Excess EDTA is added to the metal
  • solution; Unreacted EDTA is titrated with a standard metal solution.
  • d) Replacement titration: Type of complexometric titration in which the metal ion of interest cannot be
  • directly titrated with EDTA. It is replaced by another metal ion that can react with EDTA, and the
  • amount of the displaced metal ion is then determined by titration . Each type involves distinct
  • procedural steps.
  • (Principle and procedure of (a) Direct titration b) Indirect titration (c) Back titration (d) Replacement
  • titration- give 15 marks; Principle and procedure of any two with correct explanation give 10
  • marks; any one give 5 marks)
